## Suggested Readings

### General

- Farrell, S., & Lewandowsky, S. (2018). *Computational modeling of cognition and behavior.* Cambridge University Press. [eBook](https://eur.on.worldcat.org/oclc/1028902356)

### Topics

1.  **Introduction 1: R Basics**
    - [R mini tutorial](r_basics/index.html)
2.  **Introduction 2: R Basics**
    - [R mini tutorial](r_basics/index.html)
3.  **Parameter Estimation**
    - Chapter 2 of Farrell & Lewandowsky (2018), pages: 47 - 61.
    - Prince, S. J. D. (2023). Supervised learning. In [Understanding Deep Learning](https://udlbook.github.io/udlbook/) (pp. 17–24). MIT Press.
4. **Resampling & Monte Carlo Methods**
    - Chapter 2 of Farrell & Lewandowsky (2018), pages: 65 - 70.
    - Hesterberg, T., Monaghan, S., Moore, D. S., Clipson, A., & Epstein, R. (2003). [Bootstrap methods and permutation tests.](https://nhorton.people.amherst.edu/ips9/IPS_09_Ch16.pdf) In D. S. Moore, G. P. McCabe, W. M. Duckworth, & S. L. Sclove, *The practice of business statistics: Using data for decisions*. W. H. Freeman.
5.  **Neural Networks 1**
    - Hinton, G. E. (1992). How neural networks learn from experience. Scientific American, 267(3), 144-151.
    - Prince, S. J. D. (2023). Shallow neural networks. In [Understanding Deep Learning](https://udlbook.github.io/udlbook/) (pp. 25–40). MIT Press.
6.  **Neural Networks 2**
    - Section 13.2 (backpropogation) of Farrell & Lewadowsky (2018)
7. **Multinomial Processing Tree (MPT) Models**
    - *maximum likelihood estimation*: see Chapter 4 of Farrell & Lewandowsky (2018), pages: 72 - 103.
    - Schmidt, O., Erdfelder, E., & Heck, D. W. (2025). How to develop, test, and extend multinomial processing tree models: A tutorial. *Psychological Methods*, 30(4), 720–743. https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000561
    - Erdfelder, E., Auer, T.-S., Hilbig, B. E., Aßfalg, A., Moshagen, M., & Nadarevic, L. (2009). Multinomial processing tree models: A review of the literature. *Zeitschrift für Psychologie/Journal of Psychology*, 217(3), 108–124. doi: 10.1027/0044-3409.217.3.108, [download](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/220032645_Multinomial_processing_tree_models_A_review_of_the_literature)

The links above point to the online resources of the literature. Books and articles that are not listed here can be downloaded from the Canvas page.

Please note that some of the references are only accessible from the university campus. To access these materials from home, you need to set up a [VPN connection (on-campus simulation)](https://www.eur.nl/en/library/using-library/access-online-collection).
